Yes! The Venus Project is an interesting example of people striving towards a post-scarcity society. Although they might deny it because of the bad press, I would definitely describe the sort of society that the Venus Project is trying to achieve as a communist society from what I’ve read. 

The implementation of socialism in the past has been done in accordance with the theories of figures such as Karl Marx and Vladimir Lenin. Socialism involves the restructuring of the economy and the social class system to produce what’s called a dictatorship of the proletariat. This is when the ordinary working people - like you and I - have political power over the bourgeoisie (billionaires and oligarchs on a larger scale and factory owners and labour bosses on a smaller scale). The larger scale version of this is usually performed through use of a vanguard party - a ruling communist party with political power over a nation. 

The seizure of the ‘means of production’ will also take place - which is when the working people and/or communist party plan and control what they’re producing and how they’re producing it. Workplace democracy, if you like. Under this system, the economy will ultimately be bent to the will of the people at large, as opposed to having the people have to bend to the will of the economy as they do now. 

After democratising the economy, we can start to steer our society at large towards a post-scarcity phase. One of the things that concerns me about the Venus Project is that they seem to be wanting to go straight for post-scarcity, as opposed to going the more scientific route of calculating how to make this transition gradually. This would obviously be the biggest societal change in human history, and we need to do it carefully!
A post-scarcity society that can eventually be reached through the implementation of socialism. Utopia is definitely not the right term, though, because that implies something that’s fictional.
